SAMPLE SIZE.evidence_source: For Glr 15% of the variance was accounted for based on the Adjusted R-Squared by three predictors: Rated creativity in drawing (\beta = 0.35, t = 3.72, p < .001), self-reported music achievements (\beta = 0.22, t = 0.001) 2.12, p < .05), and self-reported theater and film achievements (\beta = 0.22, t = 2.19, p < .05). The model was significant at F(13, 101) = 2.53, p < .05. For Gc, 5% of the variance was accounted for based on the Adjusted R-Squared by Rated creativity in Drawing (\beta = 0.208, t = 2.17, p < .05). Model two was not significant and no additional predictors came out besides drawing so we retained the first model. The model was significant at F(2, 112) = 4.04, p < .005 (see Table 6). Hypothesis 2: When we looked at rated creativity in drawing as an outcome with Glr in block one and Gc in block two, 13% of the variance was accounted for based on the Adjusted R-Squared by one predictor: Glr (\beta = 0.371, t = 4.26, p < .001). The overall model was significant at F(2, 113) = 10.33, p < .001. The sample sizes are inferred from the F-statistics degrees of freedom: F(13, 101) implies N = 13 + 101 + 1 = 115. F(2, 112) implies N = 2 + 112 + 1 = 115. F(2, 113) implies N = 2 + 113 + 1 = 116.
